steps: In graphite, each carbon atom is covalently bonded to three other carbon atoms in flat layers.
The fourth valence electron of each carbon atom is free to move through the layers.
These mobile electrons carry electric charge, so graphite conducts electricity.
items.finalAnswer: Graphite conducts electricity because it has mobile electrons that can carry electric charge.

steps: Metal atoms are closely packed together in a regular arrangement.
The strong forces of attraction between the metal ions and the sea of mobile electrons hold the atoms firmly together, making metals usually hard.
The close packing of their particles gives metals high density, so they are usually heavy.
items.finalAnswer: Metals are usually hard and heavy because their particles are closely packed and held together by strong metallic bonding.

steps: In AlCl₃, the aluminium atom is electron-deficient and can accept a lone pair of electrons.
A chlorine atom of one AlCl₃ molecule donates a lone pair to the aluminium atom of another AlCl₃ molecule.
This forms a coordinate covalent bond; two chlorine atoms form such bonds between the molecules.
Thus, two AlCl₃ molecules join to form the dimer Al₂Cl₆.
items.finalAnswer: Two AlCl₃ molecules form Al₂Cl₆ by coordinate covalent bonds in which chlorine atoms donate lone pairs to electron-deficient aluminium atoms.

items.figure: A giant three-dimensional network of silicon and oxygen atoms, with each silicon atom bonded to four oxygen atoms and each oxygen atom linking two silicon atoms.
steps: Draw a silicon atom in the centre of a tetrahedral arrangement, surrounded by four oxygen atoms.
Join each silicon atom to its four oxygen atoms with covalent bonds.
Show each oxygen atom also bonded to another silicon atom, linking neighbouring tetrahedra throughout the structure.
Continue the pattern in all directions to represent the giant covalent structure of sand (SiO₂).
items.finalAnswer: Sand (SiO₂) has a giant three-dimensional covalent structure in which each silicon atom is bonded to four oxygen atoms, and each oxygen atom links two silicon atoms.
